evidence.title: From Modality Performance to Graceful Degradation: A PRISMA 2020 Systematic Review of Sensor Architectures for Autonomous Vehicles.
evidence.abstract: Autonomous vehicles depend on heterogeneous sensing systems whose performance varies with range, illumination, weather, object material, traffic geometry, contamination, calibration quality, and cyber-physical interference. This PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S systematic review synthesized 65 peer-reviewed primary studies selected from 2143 records identified through four databases. After removal of 793 records before screening, 1350 titles and abstracts were screened; 273 full texts were assessed and 208 were excluded with documented reasons. The final evidence base covers cameras, LiDAR, radar, thermal and event cameras, GNSS/IMU localization, calibration, synchronization, multimodal fusion, adverse-weather perception, sensor-health monitoring, and fault-tolerant perception. No modality was universally superior: comparative performance depended on hardware generation, dataset, environmental severity, range, and metric. Direct evidence was strongest for component-level perception and controlled degradation, whereas health-conditioned fusion, ODD restriction, and minimum-risk behavior were supported mainly by partial experimental evidence and safety-oriented synthesis. The review therefore proposes, rather than claims to validate, a reliability-aware architecture that separates sensor health from task confidence, preserves uncertainty and provenance, adapts fusion, and constrains operation when residual evidence is insufficient. The review was retrospectively registered in PROSPERO on 30 July 2026 (CRD420261465869).

evidence.title: Autonomous driving system for single hydrostatic transmission crawler tractor based on multi-modal steering control.
evidence.abstract: Introduction Autonomous navigation of crawler tractors is essential for precision agriculture; however, existing systems often face a trade-off between path-tracking accuracy and steering stability, particularly under complex field conditions. To address this limitation, this study aimed to develop an autonomous driving system for single-HST (Hydrostatic Transmission) crawler tractors that enhances both control resolution and operational reliability. Methods A kinematic model of the single-HST crawler chassis was established, and a state-feedback path-tracking controller integrating lateral and heading deviations was proposed. A pulse-width modulation (PWM)-based multi-modal steering control strategy was designed to enable intelligent switching and smooth transition between differential steering and unilateral braking steering by dynamically adjusting the steering hydraulic cylinder stroke. A three-layer hardware and software architecture-comprising perception, decision-making, and execution layers-was constructed, and an embedded vehicle controller integrating path planning and real-time control was developed. Field tests were conducted at the China National Precision Agriculture Research Demonstration Base, including fixed-curvature path tracking and reciprocating autonomous operation trials. Results Under curve path-tracking conditions, the proposed multi-modal steering control achieved an average lateral deviation of 4.25 cm, with a standard deviation below 5.0 cm, representing a 34.4% reduction compared with unilateral braking steering. In reciprocating operations, the average inter-row spacing error was 6.04 cm, satisfying the precision requirements for agricultural machinery under both field soil and cement pavement conditions. Discussion The results demonstrate that the proposed system effectively balances tracking accuracy and steering stability in autonomous crawler tractor navigation. The multi-modal steering strategy offers a practical solution for agricultural machinery operating on varied surfaces and shows strong potential for broader application in precision farming systems with similar terrain conditions.

evidence.title: EEG-Based Detection of Braking Intention Under Different Car Driving Conditions
evidence.abstract: The anticipatory recognition of braking is essential to prevent traffic accidents. For instance, driving assistance systems can be useful to properly respond to emergency braking situations. Moreover, the response time to emergency braking situations can be affected and even increased by different driver's cognitive states caused by stress, fatigue, and extra workload. This work investigates the detection of emergency braking from driver's electroencephalographic (EEG) signals that precede the brake pedal actuation. Bioelectrical signals were recorded while participants were driving in a car simulator while avoiding potential collisions by performing emergency braking. In addition, participants were subjected to stress, workload, and fatigue. EEG signals were classified using support vector machines (SVM) and convolutional neural networks (CNN) in order to discriminate between braking intention and normal driving. Results showed significant recognition of emergency braking intention which was on average 71.1% for SVM and 71.8% CNN. In addition, the classification accuracy for the best participant was 80.1 and 88.1% for SVM and CNN, respectively. These results show the feasibility of incorporating recognizable driver's bioelectrical responses into advanced driver-assistance systems to carry out early detection of emergency braking situations which could be useful to reduce car accidents.

system.value: Autonomous driving system for single hydrostatic transmission crawler tractor based on multi-modal steering control.

abstract.value: Introduction Autonomous navigation of crawler tractors is essential for precision agriculture; however, existing systems often face a trade-off between path-tracking accuracy and steering stability, particularly under complex field conditions. To address this limitation, this study aimed to develop an autonomous driving system for single-HST (Hydrostatic Transmission) crawler tractors that enhances both control resolution and operational reliability. Methods A kinematic model of the single-HST crawler chassis was established, and a state-feedback path-tracking controller integrating lateral and heading deviations was proposed. A pulse-width modulation (PWM)-based multi-modal steering control strategy was designed to enable intelligent switching and smooth transition between differential steering and unilateral braking steering by dynamically adjusting the steering hydraulic cylinder stroke. A three-layer hardware and software architecture-comprising perception, decision-making, and execution layers-was constructed, and an embedded vehicle controller integrating path planning and real-time control was developed. Field tests were conducted at the China National Precision Agriculture Research Demonstration Base, including fixed-curvature path tracking and reciprocating autonomous operation trials. Results Under curve path-tracking conditions, the proposed multi-modal steering control achieved an average lateral deviation of 4.25 cm, with a standard deviation below 5.0 cm, representing a 34.4% reduction compared with unilateral braking steering. In reciprocating operations, the average inter-row spacing error was 6.04 cm, satisfying the precision requirements for agricultural machinery under both field soil and cement pavement conditions. Discussion The results demonstrate that the proposed system effectively balances tracking accuracy and steering stability in autonomous crawler tractor navigation. The multi-modal steering strategy offers a practical solution for agricultural machinery operating on varied surfaces and shows strong potential for broader application in precision farming systems with similar terrain conditions.

abstract.value: The new NHSTA regulations require Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) systems to operate at night, to protect pedestrians in the deadliest conditions. We propose thermal imaging as a new sensor to complement the AEB sensor suite, alongside the visible front camera and RADAR. This paper explores the benefits of visible-thermal fusion, proposes a windshield integration for such a system, and evaluates the minimum performance requirements for a thermal camera compliant with the NHSTA standards, based on a field study of pedestrian detection range.

system.value: Implementing an Autonomous Emergency Braking with Simulink using two Radar Sensors

abstract.value: In this paper we have implemented the autonomous emergency braking using two radar sensors with different angle of coverage. The synthetic radar data is generated by radar detection generator block available in AEBTestBench simulation module. AEBTestBench is autonomous emergency simulation module available in Matlab 2018b version under ADAS toolbox. From different EURO NCAP standard scenarios available, we have covered 5 scenarios with their results analysis showing where forward collision warning is displayed and what is the AEB status. The observation of simulation results are carried out for 10 seconds. Data fusion for two radar sensors is carried by Kalman filter algorithm present inside the simulation module.

system.value: EEG-Based Detection of Braking Intention Under Different Car Driving Conditions

abstract.value: The anticipatory recognition of braking is essential to prevent traffic accidents. For instance, driving assistance systems can be useful to properly respond to emergency braking situations. Moreover, the response time to emergency braking situations can be affected and even increased by different driver's cognitive states caused by stress, fatigue, and extra workload. This work investigates the detection of emergency braking from driver's electroencephalographic (EEG) signals that precede the brake pedal actuation. Bioelectrical signals were recorded while participants were driving in a car simulator while avoiding potential collisions by performing emergency braking. In addition, participants were subjected to stress, workload, and fatigue. EEG signals were classified using support vector machines (SVM) and convolutional neural networks (CNN) in order to discriminate between braking intention and normal driving. Results showed significant recognition of emergency braking intention which was on average 71.1% for SVM and 71.8% CNN. In addition, the classification accuracy for the best participant was 80.1 and 88.1% for SVM and CNN, respectively. These results show the feasibility of incorporating recognizable driver's bioelectrical responses into advanced driver-assistance systems to carry out early detection of emergency braking situations which could be useful to reduce car accidents.

warnings.mechanism: Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough — adversarial model-uncertainty and practical-operation survival are mandatory
warnings.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-017: A discovery engine earns trust when it attacks its own successful proof harder than its unsuccessful ideas. Structural identifiability under a convenient model is not enough. A candidate must survive adversarial model uncertainty AND practical operation (safety, timing, decision value, first-pass vs post-hoc). The burden is bidirectional: (a) the proposer must demonstrate identifiability survives realistic model relaxation; (b) the killer must demonstrate non-identifiability holds under EVERY plausible estimator and measurement protocol, not just the one they chose to attack. When in doubt, the implementation is killed; the scientific question stays open until either (a) a survivor is found or (b) an explicit non-identifiability counterexample is constructed (two physically distinct latent states producing indistinguishable observations under ALL measurement protocols).

warnings.territory: Cross-cutting (extracted from Round 62 capability collision failure; applies to ALL novelty claims)
warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.mechanism: Minimum Sufficient Validation Evidence Derivation (MSVED) — 4-link chain: ML change → clinical pathway → risk envelope → minimum sufficient evidence → sufficiency proof
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

informational.mechanism: Non-Inferiority Statistical Engine (CC-08) — automated paired NI comparison with pre-registered margins for ML model modifications
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-021: Automating a standard statistical test (NI testing) for a regulatory context that explicitly requires it (PCCP) is NOT an invention. Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.mechanism: SC-05 Biofilm-Resistant Living-Surface Venous Interface — continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface with active surface-energy control at CSF-blood interface
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

custody_records.raw_content: Autonomous vehicles depend on heterogeneous sensing systems whose performance varies with range, illumination, weather, object material, traffic geometry, contamination, calibration quality, and cyber-physical interference. This PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-S systematic review synthesized 65 peer-reviewed primary studies selected from 2143 records identified through four databases. After removal of 793 records before screening, 1350 titles and abstracts were screened; 273 full texts were assessed and 208 were excluded with documented reasons. The final evidence base covers cameras, LiDAR, radar, thermal and event cameras, GNSS/IMU localization, calibration, synchronization, multimodal fusion, adverse-weather perception, sensor-health monitoring, and fault-tolerant perception. No modality was universally superior: comparative performance depended on hardware generation, dataset, environmental severity, range, and metric. Direct evidence was strongest for component-level perception and controlled degradation, whereas health-conditioned fusion, ODD restriction, and minimum-risk behavior were supported mainly by partial experimental evidence and safety-oriented synthesis. The review therefore proposes, rather than claims to validate, a reliability-aware architecture that separates sensor health from task confidence, preserves uncertainty and provenance, adapts fusion, and constrains operation when residual evidence is insufficient. The review was retrospectively registered in PROSPERO on 30 July 2026 (CRD420261465869).

custody_records.raw_content: Introduction Autonomous navigation of crawler tractors is essential for precision agriculture; however, existing systems often face a trade-off between path-tracking accuracy and steering stability, particularly under complex field conditions. To address this limitation, this study aimed to develop an autonomous driving system for single-HST (Hydrostatic Transmission) crawler tractors that enhances both control resolution and operational reliability. Methods A kinematic model of the single-HST crawler chassis was established, and a state-feedback path-tracking controller integrating lateral and heading deviations was proposed. A pulse-width modulation (PWM)-based multi-modal steering control strategy was designed to enable intelligent switching and smooth transition between differential steering and unilateral braking steering by dynamically adjusting the steering hydraulic cylinder stroke. A three-layer hardware and software architecture-comprising perception, decision-making, and execution layers-was constructed, and an embedded vehicle controller integrating path planning and real-time control was developed. Field tests were conducted at the China National Precision Agriculture Research Demonstration Base, including fixed-curvature path tracking and reciprocating autonomous operation trials. Results Under curve path-tracking conditions, the proposed multi-modal steering control achieved an average lateral deviation of 4.25 cm, with a standard deviation below 5.0 cm, representing a 34.4% reduction compared with unilateral braking steering. In reciprocating operations, the average inter-row spacing error was 6.04 cm, satisfying the precision requirements for agricultural machinery under both field soil and cement pavement conditions. Discussion The results demonstrate that the proposed system effectively balances tracking accuracy and steering stability in autonomous crawler tractor navigation. The multi-modal steering strategy offers a practical solution for agricultural machinery operating on varied surfaces and shows strong potential for broader application in precision farming systems with similar terrain conditions.

custody_records.raw_content: The anticipatory recognition of braking is essential to prevent traffic accidents. For instance, driving assistance systems can be useful to properly respond to emergency braking situations. Moreover, the response time to emergency braking situations can be affected and even increased by different driver's cognitive states caused by stress, fatigue, and extra workload. This work investigates the detection of emergency braking from driver's electroencephalographic (EEG) signals that precede the brake pedal actuation. Bioelectrical signals were recorded while participants were driving in a car simulator while avoiding potential collisions by performing emergency braking. In addition, participants were subjected to stress, workload, and fatigue. EEG signals were classified using support vector machines (SVM) and convolutional neural networks (CNN) in order to discriminate between braking intention and normal driving. Results showed significant recognition of emergency braking intention which was on average 71.1% for SVM and 71.8% CNN. In addition, the classification accuracy for the best participant was 80.1 and 88.1% for SVM and CNN, respectively. These results show the feasibility of incorporating recognizable driver's bioelectrical responses into advanced driver-assistance systems to carry out early detection of emergency braking situations which could be useful to reduce car accidents.
